I would like to share my experience as feedback for the clinic to review and improve its treatment standards.
I had a filling done, and after the procedure, I felt that my teeth were pressing against each other abnormally. I informed the dentist, and they checked and adjusted it several times. However, the dentist said that the filling area had already been ground down too low, and it was unlikely that the pressure was from the new material, but rather from another point on the same tooth unrelated to their work. They also said it was as if I was imagining it and that further correction would require grinding down my natural tooth, which they said was not advisable, but they would do if I wanted, because I would have to come back again due to my discomfort. However, it wasn't just discomfort; I really did feel the pressure. Before the procedure, there was no pressure; it only started after. But because I was worried about losing natural tooth structure, I decided against grinding. After returning home, the pressure worsened, and I experienced jaw pain on the treated side all night. The next day, I decided to seek a second opinion from a dentist I've always had treatment from, because if I went back to this clinic, I would have to undergo the grinding of my natural tooth as the dentist had previously mentioned. Normally, this dentist doesn't accept corrections from other clinics, but because I was a returning patient, they agreed. In short, the second dentist found the pressure and confirmed that I wasn't imagining it; the pressure was real and could be corrected by adjustments at this clinic. The original filling completely resolved the pressure and jaw pain without the patient having to lose any natural tooth structure, contrary to what the clinic had stated.

The purpose of this feedback is to suggest that the clinic review its approach to patient monitoring after procedures and the accuracy of bite alignment assessments, for the benefit of other patients in the future.
